variables.title: Rare-error investigation
variables.query: service.name: "${param.incident.service}" and event.outcome: "failure" and error.type: "${param.incident.error_type}" and not log.level: "WARN"

drifts.note: You filtered on the error type ${action.value}; the rare signature is easy to miss among the common ones.

demonstration.narration: Failed requests in this busy service may share one unusual error. I'll filter to those failures and drop warning-only logs so the signature is easier to spot.
demonstration.reasoning: The current window contains normal and background events. Filtering on ${var.field} reduces that noise so we can inspect the relevant records.
demonstration.evidence: The query keeps ${param.incident.service} failures and drops warning-only logs, and the hit count shows how few records remain. That small set is where the unusual signature lives.

demonstration.narration: I'll open one matching request to check its error type and trace ID together, so we have a concrete example.
demonstration.reasoning: A total can look convincing even when it includes an unrelated record. Opening a typical event checks the key values together, rather than relying on a count alone.
demonstration.evidence: This one failed ${param.incident.service} request carries ${param.incident.error_type}, so the rare error and the failures belong to the same requests. ${truth.conclusion}
